text: A cohort within the population of presenting psychiatric patients comprises individuals with serious and persistent mental illness (SPMI). Consumers within the SPMI category experience chronic, often unremitting symptomology, complex health and social issues, and substance misuse, resulting in higher emergency service utilisation ( 1 , 7 , 8 ). This subset of patients is usually supported through a case management framework that aims to address biopsychosocial needs outside a crisis setting ( 9 ). A key feature of case management is that it is provided during business hours (Monday–Friday), which has previously been described as a limitation in servicing the SPMI cohort ( 9 ).
source_label: Assertive community treatment for adults with complex mental illness and emergency department use: a systematic review
